newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on oil deal demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on oil deal demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly lower against its American counterpart on Thursday on U.S. dollar demand from the state-run Chinese Petroleum Corp to purchase oil, dealers said.
Dealers estimated the state oil firm's U.S. dollar demand as worth some US$60 million.
The local dollar ended at an intraday low of T$27.503, against Wednesday's T$27.501 close. Turnover through dealers was a modest US$147 million.
"The local dollar's closing lower was also reflecting the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas," said one dealer.
"On the other hand, investors had actively supplied U.S. dollars, thus offsetting the Taiwan dollar's depreciation," the dealer said.
Dealers said they expected narrow-range trading to continue in coming sessions despite emerging year-end U.S. dollar demand.
For Friday, a T$27.495-T$27.515 range was seen.
